title: The tester’s mindset: hypothesis, evidence and reproduction

videos.script: On Monday, the box office passes on a complaint. A family was overcharged on Sunday morning. {{complaint}} That sentence is true, and nearly useless. It says something went wrong, and nothing about what. {{useless}} This lesson is about the distance between a complaint like that, and two commands anybody can run to see the defect. {{distance}} The method is old. Write down what was observed. List every explanation that fits. Then run the experiments whose results could prove each one wrong. {{method}} Sunday? One run rules it out. The hour? Another run. The way the hour was written? That one survives. {{experiments}} And it is a defect that was in the code from the first day, waiting for a session that started before ten. {{waiting}} Along the way, a distinction that changes how teams treat testers. Doubt the claim, never the person who made it. {{end}}
